custom_logic_notes: Two variants exist: v1 (negative_spread.mq5) uses OnTick with market orders (ORDER_TYPE_SELL) when negative spread detected, then immediately closes position via CTrade.PositionClose. v2 (negative_spread_forts.mq5) uses OnBookEvent with DOM depth data, places SELL_LIMIT at bid when no position and negative spread exists, then enters a busy-wait loop deleting the limit order if bid price changes before position fills. When position exists, places BUY_LIMIT at ask to close, with same busy-wait deletion logic. The FORTS version subscribes to market book (DOM) via MarketBookAdd and uses MarketBookGet for real-time bid/ask from order book rather than SymbolInfoDouble. The core strategy exploits negative spread anomalies (ask < bid) to guarantee risk-free entry. The busy-wait loops (while(i==PositionsTotal())) are problematic design - they block the EA thread waiting for position fill, deleting the pending order if the DOM price moves away from the order price. This is a high-frequency scalping strategy that requires tick-level DOM data and low-latency execution, making it unsuitable for standard bar-based backtesting.
python_conversion_notes: This EA is fundamentally incompatible with standard Python backtesting frameworks (backtrader, vectorbt, etc.) because: (1) It relies on DOM/Level-2 order book data via MarketBookGet, which is not available in typical OHLCV datasets. (2) The core signal is a negative spread (ask<bid) which is an ultra-transient market microstructure anomaly requiring tick-by-tick bid/ask data with sub-millisecond resolution. (3) The busy-wait loop pattern (while(PositionsTotal()==i)) is an anti-pattern that cannot be replicated in event-driven backtest engines. (4) The FORTS variant specifically targets Russian derivatives exchange with specific order filling rules (ORDER_FILLING_RETURN). A Python conversion would need: custom tick-level data feed with full DOM snapshots, a simulated order matching engine that can produce negative spreads, and an event loop that handles pending order placement/cancellation within the same tick. The v1 variant is simpler (market orders on negative spread, immediate close) and could be approximated with tick data containing bid/ask, but the edge relies on execution speed impossible to simulate accurately.
